title: Benton-Frederick bike lanes and Wilmot farm crop motion
subtitle: Downtown waste collection concerns, Sustainable Waterloo Region update, Snyder's Road East parking ban, and deferred agenda items.
overview: The committee recommended Phase 1 cycling improvements on Benton and Frederick streets in Kitchener. Four travel lanes would become two, with painted bike lanes added and parking rules changed along the corridor. Staff were also directed to develop a long-term plan for separated cycling facilities and better pedestrian and cycling access to the Frederick ION station.

Before the delegations, a motion that came out of a closed session was brought to open session and carried {{vote:m1}}. It responds to the Region plowing under a corn crop on a 160-acre Wilmot Township farm bought for industrial land assembly. It sets out how crops on future purchases will be handled and requires a public report within four weeks. Council is also to get advance notice of further work on those lands.

The committee also recommended a no-parking zone on part of Snyder's Road East in Wilmot. It heard from Sustainable Waterloo Region and from business improvement area directors about downtown garbage collection. Because the meeting ran well past its scheduled time and several members were absent, the remaining regular agenda items were deferred to August 28, 2024.

decisions.item: Wilmot farm crop and land assembly
decisions.detail: Committee carried a motion committing the Region to assess whether crops on further farms bought through the land assembly can be harvested before any action, requiring a public report within four weeks on the plowed corn crop, and giving Council advance notice of further work on those lands.

The committee recommended reducing Benton and Frederick streets from four lanes to two and adding painted bicycle lanes, with related parking and stopping changes to the Traffic and Parking By-law {{vote:m3}}.

As part of the same motion, the committee recommended that staff develop a long-term plan for separated cycling facilities and better pedestrian and cycling access to the Frederick ION station, to be built when the streets are reconstructed.
The committee recommended adding a no-parking-anytime zone on both sides of Snyder's Road East in Wilmot, from 1.2 km east of Notre Dame Road to 1.8 km west of Trussler Road {{vote:m4}}.

debate: Delegates from cycling and neighbourhood groups supported the Benton-Frederick plan, citing safer crossings and slower speeds, and urged the Region to move quickly to Phase 2.

A cycling advocacy delegate and another resident asked for physically separated lanes rather than paint, saying painted lanes might not stop drivers from passing or cutting into them. The advocacy group said concrete dividers would fit within the project budget.
Delegates also asked that Phase 1 cover the middle section between Charles and Weber streets, arguing a gap would discourage cycling. They suggested painted lanes there as a pilot.

A condominium representative supported bike lanes but raised concerns about where service and moving vehicles could stop. The building has no visitor parking, and the delegate said staff had not contacted the condominium directly.

Business improvement area directors supported the Region staying responsible for downtown waste collection, but said a one-size-fits-all approach would not work. They were concerned about moving from six-day to two-day pickup, asked for a phased approach with more data, and asked for collaboration with the Region.
